name: AAGAM PR Review + Autofix
prompt:
You are running as an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Saikumar-bali, the owner of Saikumar-bali/AAGAM_E-commerce. Review this pull request AND fix the real problems the review finds.

STEP 0 - GATE (before anything else).
Read the GitHub event payload above. If the PR is not from Saikumar-bali/AAGAM_E-commerce, or the PR author is not Saikumar-bali, or the PR head repository is a fork (pull_request.head.repo.fork == true), STOP immediately and do nothing. Do not comment, do not push. Output only: 'SKIPPED: not an owner-authored PR in the target repo.'

STEP 1 - CONFIRM HEAD. Use /pr-reviewer:setup if available, otherwise proceed with gh directly.
Run: gh pr view <number> --json number,title,body,headRefName,headRefOid,baseRefName,additions,deletions,changedFiles,labels
The repository is cloned at main in the working directory. In the repository directory run: git fetch origin pull/<number>/head:pr-<number> && git checkout pr-<number>. Then confirm `git rev-parse HEAD` matches the PR head SHA before you review anything. If the fetch fails, stop and report that rather than reviewing stale code.
Never push to main or master.

STEP 2 - READ THE PR. Read the changed files from that checkout, cross-checked with `gh pr diff <number>`. This is a TypeScript monorepo: NestJS api-gateway, Next.js admin-dashboard, Expo mobile-customer and mobile-partners, Prisma in packages/database.

STEP 3 - REVIEW using the code-review skill. Priority order:
1. Correctness and data-structure bugs: off-by-one, sequence/count derivation, uniqueness-constraint collisions, missing transaction boundaries, and re-reads inside transactions that drop ownership checks.
2. Money and ledger accounting: paise arithmetic, increment vs set, idempotency keys, double counting, entitlements and funding consumption.
3. Security: authorization and ownership checks, input validation, unsafe key/url construction, secrets, injection.
4. Breaking changes to existing API or behaviour, and whether tests were updated.
5. PR description claims that do not match the code (a described cron/scheduler that is not wired up, migrations claimed as applied, etc).
Ignore pure formatting and style; linters handle that. Do not manufacture feedback. If the PR is genuinely good, say so and stop.
Before claiming something is missing, grep the repo and read the file - a diff summary is often incomplete.
Verify every line number you cite with `sed -n` before using it.

STEP 4 - PUBLISH THE REVIEW with gh api (POST /repos/Saikumar-bali/AAGAM_E-commerce/pulls/<number>/reviews). Body: a taste rating, grouped findings (critical / improvements / testing gaps), a risk assessment, and a verdict. Be blunt and specific: cite file:line and explain the consequence. Include the line: '_This review was generated by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Saikumar-bali._'
Then add inline comments for each file:line finding. Verify each line is an added line in the PR diff first - a comment on a non-diff line is rejected with a 422.
If the authenticated token is the PR author, GitHub rejects APPROVE and REQUEST_CHANGES, so use event=COMMENT.

STEP 5 - FIX WHAT IS UNAMBIGUOUS.
Fix only findings that are clearly correct and low-risk: failing tests this PR itself broke, missing null/ownership checks, wrong sequence or uniqueness derivation, non-idempotent keys, paise increment-vs-set errors, and missing entitlement/funding calls that sibling branches already make.
Do NOT guess on business-policy changes, unverifiable payment semantics, destructive migrations, or anything needing a product decision. Report those as 'needs a human decision' in the PR comment instead.

STEP 6 - VERIFY. Run `npm run test:ci --workspace=apps/api-gateway` at minimum, plus `npx prisma validate --schema packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma` if the schema changed. Note the suite needs a reachable Postgres (DATABASE_URL); if it is unavailable, say so explicitly rather than reporting a pass. If a change breaks a test, fix the code - or update the test if the test encodes outdated behaviour, and say which you did and why. Never leave the branch with failing tests of your own making.

STEP 7 - PUSH. Create or switch to a branch, commit with a clear message, and push. Append this trailer to the commit message: 'Co-authored-by: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev>'. Do not force-push a shared branch and do not merge the PR.

STEP 8 - REPORT. Post one PR comment: what you reviewed, what you fixed (with commit sha), what you deliberately did not fix and why, and the current CI status. Do not mark the PR ready for review.

If you cannot complete a step, say so plainly rather than reporting success. Never report work you did not do.
